security_spec.violation_condition: When QEMU delivers an interrupt via CLIC IVT (Interrupt Vector Table) mode, the emulation reads the handler address from VTBASE but does NOT clear the corresponding interrupt-pending bit (clicintip[i]) for the serviced interrupt before setting PC, OR unconditionally clears it for level-sensitive interrupts where the spec mandates 'if possible' semantics, meaning level-sensitive interrupts may remain pending due to the external source still asserting the level.
security_spec.summary: IVT mode trap delivery must auto-clear the serviced interrupt's pending bit upon successful handler-address fetch; missing this side-effect causes the interrupt to repeatedly re-fire, effectively hanging the guest in an interrupt storm (DoS).

findings.finding: S-mode vectored interrupt path: uses stvec for handler address calculation. No CLIC IVT (stvec bits[1:0]==3) support exists, so there is no IVT pending-bit auto-clear logic to audit. The existing vectored mode (bits[1:0]==1) uses standard trap model where software clears pending bits via CSR writes — no auto-clear is expected per the privileged spec.

M-mode vectored interrupt path: same as S-mode — uses mtvec with standard vectored mode. No IVT (bits[1:0]==3) handling exists. The standard vectored mode does not require auto-clearing pending bits; software ISR handles this via mip CSR writes.

The entire riscv_cpu_do_interrupt() function — from entry to PC assignment — never touches env->mip or any pending bits. In the standard RISC-V privileged architecture model (the only model implemented), this is correct: interrupt pending bits are cleared by software writing to mip in the ISR, not by the hardware trap delivery path. No missing auto-clear bug exists because the CLIC/IVT feature is not implemented.

findings.finding: write_mtvec rejects reserved mode bits[1:0] >= 2. This means CLIC IVT mode (bits[1:0]==3) is correctly rejected as unimplemented rather than silently accepted with broken behavior. This is safe.
